research_value: This objective tests whether addition and multiplication can be treated through a common defect/coordinate/spectral language rather than as unrelated primitives. Even a negative result is valuable if it sharply classifies where exact translation fails and what information must be retained.
scope: Classify exact, discrete and finite-resolution bridges between addition and multiplication. Primary routes are integer binomial cross-effects, prime-indexed delta/Frobenius defects, formal-group interpolation, finite Witt/ghost coordinates, valuation/tropical collapse, finite-field additive–multiplicative spectra, and obstruction/stress theorems. External classical theories are comparison models to be translated or bounded, not automatic native foundations.
